title: Aetna / Applied Extrusion / Aether / Ampex / ADDvantage / AudioEye — Forecast, Security Selection, Asset Floors and Growth Duration V9

notes: AET 2000, AET 2009 and AETC 2001 raw Short -> actual Long.
AETH Corp 2001 is not a common-equity idea; it is a Long in Aether Systems 6% convertible subordinated notes due 2005.
Aetna 2000 is evaluated using the ING breakup consideration: approximately $35.33 cash per old Aetna share plus one share of the new health company.
AETC refinancing succeeded through a $275m 10.75% senior-notes issue, but operating economics failed and existing common was later cancelled in Chapter 11.
Aether's 6% notes were redeemed in 2004 at 101.2% of par plus accrued interest; exact realized IRR is not asserted without full settlement/coupon dates.
Ampex existing common was cancelled in its 2008 restructuring; contingent payment rights are not treated as preservation of the old common-equity thesis.

AEY 2010, 2013 and 2018 are kept as separate tactical idea units. ADDvantage later ceased operations and filed Chapter 7 in January 2024, demonstrating that historical NCAV/tangible book was not a permanent floor.
AudioEye's early price rerating and gross-margin thesis were successful, but the original 3-4 year ~$50m revenue path was too aggressive; 2024 revenue was $35.2m and 2025 revenue $40.3m.

meta.one_line_verdict_ko: partner distribution·GM expansion과 2021초 price rerating은 강하게 성공했지만 3~4Y $50m revenue duration forecast는 과대

batch_lessons: A breakup transaction can validate one SOTP leg without validating the valuation assigned to the remaining stub.
Aetna 2006 demonstrates that forecasting earnings correctly does not guarantee a correct stock-price forecast when the valuation regime changes.
Managed-care membership growth and medical-cost margin must be analyzed separately.
Refinancing repairs liquidity, not operating economics or solvency; AETC refinanced successfully and still wiped out common equity.
Aether demonstrates the opposite security-selection lesson: a weak company can produce an excellent debt return when discounted claims are cash-covered.
Patent-royalty income should be modeled contract by contract with expiry, renewal and debt-waterfall risk rather than as a perpetual high-margin annuity.
NCAV and tangible book are not permanent floors when inventory can obsolete, receivables can deteriorate and operating losses consume cash.
Asset plays without liquidation or monetization catalysts should carry a time-decay haircut.
AudioEye shows that high-growth SaaS forecasts require separate assumptions for growth rate and growth duration.
Price-target attainment, operating-mechanism success and terminal security outcome should remain separate fields.
